flawed_step: The claim incorrectly infers that requiring no swaps makes an already-sorted array cheap; runtime is measured by key comparisons, and first-element pivot selection produces maximally unbalanced partitions.
counterexample: For every n≥1, take A_n=[1,2,...,n]. The first pivot is always the smallest element, so partitioning a subarray of size k makes k−1 key comparisons and leaves a recursive subarray of size k−1. Thus the total is (n−1)+(n−2)+⋯+1=n(n−1)/2 comparisons, which is Θ(n²) and not O(n log n).
assessment_summary: The explicit infinite family of ascending sorted arrays violates the claimed worst-case O(n log n) bound.
